title: Protocol at a Glance
description: Start with the README narrative: pactify is a portable multi-agent coordination protocol where a git-tracked append-only event log (.pact/log.jsonl) is authoritative and STATE.yml is a regenerable projection. The formal spec defines events, roles, and the two invariants. Read these before any code to understand the story the rest of the tour retells through actual structure.

title: The Event Log — the single source of truth
description: The heart of the protocol lives in internal/event. An Event carries verb/actor/task/feature payloads; log.go appends events (stamping id + timestamp) and reads them back losslessly. Everything else is derived from this JSONL file, so understanding Append/ReadAll and the Event shape is foundational.

title: Projection — folding events into STATE.yml
description: internal/projection turns the log into state. Project/Fold replays events into the State/Feature/Task/Seat model; render.go serializes it byte-aligned to STATE.yml; snapshot.go accelerates replays. This is the 'log is source, STATE is projection, CLI recomputes' rule made concrete.

title: Rules — the two invariants enforced
description: rules.go encodes the protocol guarantees: a worker cannot self-accept (only the task's reviewer can), and a feature cannot merge until all its tasks are accepted. checkCheckpoint, checkReviewerVerdict, checkMerge, and the role gate are where correctness is guarded before any event is written.

title: The Engine — verbs that mutate the ledger
description: engine.go is the transactional core: each protocol verb (assign, start, checkpoint, changes, accept, merge, join) runs under a ledger lock, checks rules, then appends-and-renders atomically. This is where log, projection, and rules compose into safe state transitions.

title: Seats & Roles — who may act
description: seat.go models agent identities (seats) and their roles, and manages the pact-managed block baked into AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md. Combined with the role gate, seats decide which verbs an actor may perform — the identity layer behind the invariants.

title: The CLI Surface
description: cmd/pactify is the standard implementation of the protocol. main.go wires the root command; commands.go assembles subcommands (setup, join, assign, checkpoint, run, serve, mcp, orchestrate...). This is the primary human/agent entry point that drives the engine.

title: Orchestration Engine — driving agents automatically
description: internal/orchestrate runs the pull-based dispatch loop: it reads STATE, launches owner and reviewer agents, runs gates, handles rework/escalation, and merges when green. loop.go's Run is mission control's automation brain, turning the protocol into a self-driving workflow.

title: MCP Server — protocol as agent tools
description: internal/mcp exposes the protocol over the Model Context Protocol so any MCP-capable agent can participate. server.go serves tools (status/join/assign/checkpoint/accept/merge) and resources (pact://state, pact://log); tools.go registers them and resolves the target project.

title: Web Dashboard — mission control
description: web/ is the React+Vite dashboard. main.tsx boots the app, App.tsx composes the views, lib/api.ts talks to the serve API, and Canvas.tsx renders the live board. Per the canvas craft spec, node positions have exactly two writers and RF nodes only merge-by-id.

title: Cloud Relay — remote coordination
description: Cloud lets seats coordinate across machines. Go-side internal/cloudclient authenticates and holds sessions while internal/relaysock speaks the wire protocol; the TS relay server (cloud/relay) and relay-client persist and broadcast events. This mirrors the local engine over the network.

title: CI/CD, Release & Tests
description: The distribution and verification layer: ci.yml runs Go + web unit tests and Playwright e2e; release.yml + .goreleaser.yaml build the single static binary; install.sh delivers it. Protocol behavior is pinned by bats suites (protocol_v1, merge, checkpoint) plus web vitest — the double-green gate.
